fig01.hint: Hover over or tap a phase or an event to highlight the matching point below.

tl1.title: 1947–1971: wars and treaties
tl1.note: J&K war (1947–48), IWT (1960), Tashkent (1966), the 1971 war and Bangladesh.

tl2.title: 1972: Shimla Agreement
tl2.note: Ceasefire line converted into the LoC; bilateralism written in.

tl4.title: 1999–2008: peace process with shocks
tl4.note: Lahore and Kargil (1999), LoC ceasefire (2003), Composite Dialogue.

tl5.title: 2008–2019: stop–start
tl5.note: 26/11 (2008), Uri and surgical strikes (2016), Pulwama, Balakot and Article 370 (2019).

tl6.title: 2019–2025: cold peace
tl6.note: DGMO ceasefire recommitment (February 2021); Kartarpur; no political dialogue.

tl7.title: 2025 onwards: new normal
tl7.note: Pahalgam, IWT abeyance, Operation Sindoor and the 10 May ceasefire.

fig02.hint: Hover over or tap the bars to highlight the matching point.

trade.title: Exports to Pakistan
trade.note: US$ 2.07 bn in 2018-19, falling after MFN withdrawal (2019); about US$ 0.12 bn in May–October 2025, mostly medicines.

importban.title: Import ban, 2 May 2025
importban.note: All direct and indirect imports from Pakistan banned after Pahalgam; the 2025-26 bar covers May–October only.

fig04.hint: Hover over or tap a crisis column to highlight the matching points.

ladder.title: Escalation after major attacks
ladder.note: Uri 2016: surgical strikes (rung 3). Pulwama 2019: Balakot (rung 4). Pahalgam 2025: terror camps, then 11 air bases (rung 5); each crisis climbed higher.

fig05.hint: Hover over or tap an argument to highlight the matching point.

goodwill.title: Terror destroys treaty goodwill
goodwill.note: A state sponsoring terror cannot claim the benefits of a treaty built on good faith.

changed.title: Changed circumstances
changed.note: Article XII(3) notices (2023, 2024); suspension for a fundamental change (VCLT Art. 62).

projects.title: Faster projects for J&K
projects.note: Pakal Dul, Kiru, Kwar, Ratle and Sawalkot fast-tracked: power and irrigation gains.

leverage.title: Leverage against a terror sponsor
leverage.note: Abeyance as lasting leverage vs an "IWT 2.0" with climate data and one dispute track.

noexit.title: No exit clause
noexit.note: The treaty has no exit clause; obligations bind (pacta sunt servanda, VCLT Art. 26).

coa.title: Court of Arbitration award
coa.note: 31 August 2026: no unilateral suspension; India rejects the court, but risks legal isolation.

storage.title: Little storage
storage.note: India has little storage on the Western rivers, so short-term leverage is small.

precedent.title: Brahmaputra precedent
precedent.note: India is a lower riparian on the Brahmaputra, where China began a large dam in July 2025.

fig06.hint: Hover over or tap a country to highlight the matching points.

india.title: India
india.note: Builds a route around Pakistan through Afghanistan (Kabul embassy, October 2025) and Iran (Chabahar).

china.title: China
china.note: Arms, CPEC, UN "technical holds" and live inputs in May 2025, yet signed the SCO condemnation of Pahalgam.

us.title: United States
us.note: Claimed credit for the 10 May ceasefire (India denies), courted Pakistan’s army chief, cut tariffs on Pakistan.

pak.title: Pakistan
pak.note: 27th Amendment (November 2025): the army chief is also Chief of Defence Forces.

fig03.hint: Hover over or tap a marker, line or river to highlight the matching point.

ib.title: International Border
ib.note: About 2,400 km from Gujarat through Rajasthan and Punjab to Jammu; fenced, guarded by the BSF.

loc.title: Line of Control
loc.note: About 740 km military line from the Shimla Agreement; guarded by the Army.

agpl.title: AGPL, Siachen
agpl.note: About 110 km on the Saltoro Ridge north of NJ9842; held by India since Op Meghdoot (1984).

sircreek.title: Sir Creek
sircreek.note: 96 km tidal estuary in the Rann of Kutch; the boundary decides the maritime boundary and EEZs.

cpec.title: CPEC
cpec.note: Khunjerab Pass through Gilgit-Baltistan to Gwadar near Hormuz; India opposes it as a violation of sovereignty.

rivers.title: Indus rivers
rivers.note: Indus, Jhelum and Chenab (Western) and Ravi, Beas and Sutlej (Eastern); the Western rivers cross Indian territory first.

crossings.title: Attari–Wagah and Kartarpur
crossings.note: The only crossings for people and goods; both closed since 2025.
